title: A-Pillar Trim Panel — Convertible
introduction:
The convertible’s A-pillar trim comes off after the sun visor, with separate retainers along the pillar and clips at its lower end. I use the drawings as an attachment map: this is more like unbuttoning a jacket than peeling off a sticker. Release each attachment in order and account for any wiring before taking the part away.

This procedure applies to the convertible. It includes the optional visor and speaker connections, then refits the parts in reverse order. The visor drawing shows a rotational release at its pivot; it does not establish a universal downward or upward rotation direction.

items.name: Speaker operation controls, if a speaker is fitted
items.detail: If this trim has a speaker, confirm before dismantling that the radio matches either the documented non-touchscreen SYNC controls (VOL/Power, RADIO, TUNE and Seek) or MyFord Touch (Home screen, lower-left Entertainment corner, AM/FM tabs, Power, VOL, TUNE and Seek). The completion check below covers those interfaces only. If the fitted interface differs, stop before dismantling and obtain its complete matching operating instructions. No other interface is covered here. If no speaker is fitted, omit the speaker connector and audio-check branch.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Wear the required protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the required protection may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: Remove the Visor and Pillar Trim
NOTE: The illustrations show LHD (left-hand drive); RHD (right-hand drive) is similar.
edits.why: Use the attachment locations as your guide when working with the other steering layout.

edits.text: NOTE: The RH (right-hand) side is shown; the LH (left-hand) side is similar.
edits.why: The illustrated side does not limit the procedure to that side of the vehicle.

edits.text: Remove the sun visor using the cap, clip and pivot-release sequence below.
edits.why: The visor mounting is removed before the pillar trim. Its optional electrical connection is disconnected after the mounting is released.

edits.text: Remove the sun visor cap covering the pivot mounting.
edits.why: Removing this cover exposes the retaining clip shown in the enlarged mounting view.

edits.text: Release the retaining clip at the exposed sun visor pivot mounting.
edits.why: This clip locks the mounting in place. It must be released before the rotational removal movement.

edits.text: Rotate the sun visor mounting around its pivot as shown by the curved arrow to disengage it, then remove the visor from its mounting location.
edits.why: The drawing establishes rotation at the pivot, rather than a straight pull. I use that movement without assigning a downward or upward direction that the view does not establish.

edits.text: If equipped with an electrical connection, disconnect the sun visor connector before taking the released visor away.
edits.why: The enlarged connector view identifies the remaining connection at the visor mounting. Releasing the mounting does not also disconnect its wiring.

edits.text: Remove the A-pillar trim panel using the retainer, optional speaker-connector and lower-clip sequence below.
edits.why: The panel has attachments along its length as well as at its lower end. Releasing the visible upper portion alone does not free the whole panel.

edits.text: Pull the trim away from the pillar at the indicated attachment locations to release its retainers.
edits.why: The drawing identifies the retainers near the top and along the panel, with enlarged views of their shapes. At this stage, leave the lower end attached while addressing any speaker connection.

edits.text: If equipped with a speaker, disconnect its electrical connector behind the released trim panel.
edits.why: The connector attaches to the rear of the speaker near the lower portion of the trim. Disconnecting it before the final release keeps the panel from remaining tethered by its wiring.

edits.text: Release the remaining clips at the lower end, free the panel from the instrument-panel edge and remove the A-pillar trim panel.
edits.why: The final arrow is at the panel's base. This completes the release after the upper retainers and any speaker wiring have been addressed.

edits.text: Refit the Pillar Trim and Visor

Install by reversing the removal sequence. Position the pillar trim and engage its lower clips, reconnect the speaker connector if equipped, then engage the retainers along the pillar. Reconnect the sun visor electrical connector if equipped, refit the visor by reversing its mounting rotation, engage the retaining clip and reinstall the cap.
edits.why:
The reverse order restores each electrical connection before its part is fully secured. I account for the lower clips, pillar retainers and visor lock separately; a panel that looks aligned still needs every disturbed attachment restored.

After the trim, visor, cap and every fitted connector are restored, check that the disturbed attachments hold securely and no wire is trapped by the trim. Keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and engine stopped. Bring the valid key inside; from confirmed ignition OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal for engine-off ON. If the visor has an illuminated vanity mirror, lift its mirror cover to switch the lamp on and check that it illuminates, then close the cover again. This is the ordinary mirror cover, not the mounting cap removed during the repair.

If the pillar speaker was disconnected, check ordinary playback using the interface matched before work. On non-touchscreen SYNC, if audio is OFF press VOL/Power; if already ON leave it ON. Press RADIO, then use TUNE or Seek to find a familiar station and turn VOL to a comfortable level. On MyFord Touch, if audio is OFF press Power; if already ON leave it ON. Touch Home, then the lower-left Entertainment corner and AM or FM; use TUNE or Seek and adjust VOL. Listen for sound from the disturbed speaker. After the check, press the applicable audio Power control to turn audio OFF. Whether or not optional equipment was present, finish by pressing and releasing START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key and keep the parking brake and parked gear in place. These are ordinary completion checks, not electrical fault isolation. If a connection, lamp, speaker or attachment is abnormal, stop before driving and keep ignition OFF/key out before reopening the trim. See the [matching owner manual, Sun Visors, Audio and Starting](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for the fitted controls.

editorialRevision.scope: Add known parked ignition preparation and conditional owner-backed visor-lamp/audio completion with matched interface before work. Preserve all primary removal/refit text including direction-neutral visor rotation and optional connector branches. Full prior review retained; independent bounded review recorded separately.
